data.Description: Matthew Lyrek pointed a handgun at deputies outside the Dollar General in his hometown of Montrose in 2024.
data.Story:
A man has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for a standoff with police outside a Dollar General store in his hometown, which ended with him being shot by deputies.

Matthew Lyrek was found guilty in July of 11 charges – including four counts of first-degree assault – following the Apr. 15, 2024 standoff in the parking lot outside the convenience store in Montrose, Wright County.

Wright County deputies were attempting to arrest Lyrek on outstanding warrants including two violations of orders of protection, and an outstanding warrant for threats of violence, fleeing police, and obstruction relating to an incident less than two weeks earlier in which he threatened to shoot police officers.

Police learned Lyrek was shopping at the Dollar General at 631 Nelson Blvd., but as he exited the store and got into his truck, Lyrek pulled a loaded handgun from his waistband and pointed it at the approaching deputies.

The deputies initially used Tasers in an attempt to arrest Lyrek, but he continued pointing the gun at deputies, eventually culminating with two deputies shooting him.

Even after being shot, Lyrek continued to aim his gun at law enforcement, with bean bag and foam rounds being used, causing him to drop the gun, though deputies arresting him found another gun still in his waistband.

Lyrek was hospitalized with gunshot wounds to his abdomen and back.

A subsequent search of his home turned up at least five firearms and an “arsenal of ammunition” comprising more than 29,000 rounds.

“Thank you to the courageous deputies with the Wright County Sheriff’s Office who responded to apprehend Lyrek, knowing he was armed and dangerous,” said Wright County Attorney Brian Lutes.

“The deputies risked their lives to keep the citizens of Wright County safe.”

USING A HAMMER TO KILL HIS FATHER
data.Description: The 29-year-old's mother say he has schizophrenia and recently changed his medication.
data.Story:
A man has been charged with using a hammer to kill his father at their home in North St. Paul, with the victim’s wife saying their son had recently changed his medications for schizophrenia.

Charges in Ramsey County allege that Jamal Nash, 29, struck his 69-year-old father in the head with a hammer at around 1:30 p.m. Sunday on the 2700 block of Chippewa Avenue. He died from his injuries at Regions Hospital on Monday.

Police were called to the home by Nash’s mother, who was holding a bloody towel and led responders to her husband. He was unresponsive and “bled profusely from his head,” according to the criminal complaint.

Nash’s mother said her son, who had fled out of the back door, had been diagnosed with schizophrenia five years ago, and had recently changed medications that caused changes in his behavior.

She said he had been stressed, stayed awake for days, had stopped eating, and would “pace the floor.” She said her son had never been aggressive or violent in the past, and loved his father.

She further told police that Nash had been in the hospital the previous week after they found him having a seizure. He called them asking to be picked up the next day, but a doctor she spoke to had wanted him to stay in the hospital for longer to determine if the medicine was changing his behavior.

Nash’s mother says he lied to her about doctors approving his release from the hospital. He moved in with his parents on Saturday, the day before the attack.

On Sunday, Nash’s father set up a TV in Nash’s bedroom and then went to the living room to unpack more items. Nash’s mother said she saw her son come out of his room and swing the hammer at his father without warning or any prior argument.

The father tried to grab the ball peen hammer, but he swung it at him again. The father was struck twice on the side of the head.

In the wake of the attack, Nash allegedly said “Oh my God” and started crying and screaming, before fleeing the house. Police caught up with him a short time later after Nash told his brother where he was during a phone call.

After agreeing to speak to police, Nash was asked what happened, and said: “Someone was attacking my whole family.” He didn’t respond when asked who attacked his family, but later said: “Somebody hit my father, and my mother was crying.”

He then said the incident was an accident, and when asked to tell his side of the story, he allegedly said: “I hit my father. He was holding me for hostage.”
